Secondary batteries · Commercial

Lithium iron phosphate · LFP

During discharge, lithium ions leave graphite and enter the cathode's iron-phosphate structure, while electrons pass through the external circuit. Charging reverses both flows.

Animated operating principles

Ion and electron pathways

Li⁺ · electrolyte / membrane Electrons e⁻ · external circuit

Simplified reaction directions and pathways. Actual particle numbers and speeds differ.

Electrode and electrolyte principles

Organic solvent with dissolved lithium salts. Li⁺ moves surrounded by solvent molecules and desolvates at electrode surfaces.

Discharge: LiC₆ → C₆ + Li⁺ + e⁻ / FePO₄ + Li⁺ + e⁻ → LiFePO₄

Advantages

No nickel or cobalt, with generally good life and thermal stability.

Drawbacks & challenges

Less stored energy per unit mass or volume than high-nickel chemistries in many designs; low-temperature limitations.

Materials & supply constraints

Lithium, iron phosphate and graphite. Calling this a rare-earth technology is inaccurate.

Main applications

Affordable EVs, buses and stationary ESS
